keyFindings.description: A handle's refusal does not latch: acting() re-evaluates on every step, so a task that caught a StepRefused passes its next step once its session is open again. reconcileNow's inbound catch (envoy.ts:2445-2451) and settleRole's catch (envoy.ts:2586-2600) then go on to register, settle the role and throw InboundError or log 'role reclaim failed', where main ended the pass at the first refusal. Latch the refusal (guard, dial, and claimRole's two direct throws) and add an A1 test.

subscribe and watchAgentStream lost main's `if (!live()) return` after `await ensureConnection(...)` (main envoy.ts:1755-1758, 2061-2064). handle.dial checks only after the raw dial; ensureConnection then awaits dialled.close() when another caller won the connection (envoy.ts:975-977), and a refusal there lets a refused task open subjects and overwrite agentStreamControl. handle.subscribe's after-guard throws only once the subjects are open.

recoverRegisteredInterests makes a listener request (client.unsubscribe) inside a queued task outside the handle, fenced by hand-written handle.check() calls at 2231 and 2249. R2: each listener request after a wait goes through the handle.

sessionLeftDuringClaim tells the Legion bridge and envoy_role_set 'nothing was claimed' also when the listener granted the claim and claimRole adopted it after the session moved (registration-state.ts:555-565). Main told the two apart. The model is told nothing was claimed while the listener holds the claim.

Twelve handle.check() calls remain, and six of them (2505, 2512, 2519, 2524, 2578, 2598) guard nothing a following handle step does not guard itself, while registration-state.ts:18,108 and envoy.ts:2033 say no call site re-checks a fence. Remove the redundant ones and say in those comments where check() is still needed.

No `## Contract change census`, while the PR changes a package-boundary signature (@legion/envoy-client unregisterSession), adds a response body to DELETE /v1/sessions/<id>, and adds a refusal (a soft claim naming a live predecessor of another instance now answers 409).

A second lost compare-and-swap answers deleted=false with reason 'the registration belongs to another client instance', which can be false (the common cause is the same instance's heartbeat). Give that case its own reason.

On a json.Unmarshal type error `stored` can be partly filled, so a malformed value can still carry a ClientInstanceID and be kept, against the comment that it is deleted as an entry with no id. Zero stored on error.
The predecessor decision is a switch three levels deep in roleSetHandler, and the log condition repeats InstanceMatches's empty-id rule. Move it into one function beside liveSessionEntry.
